evals.prompt: I'm brand new to Algolia and don't have an account yet. Get me set up from scratch so I have an App ID and API key I can use.
evals.expected_output: A quickstart flow: ensure the CLI is installed, create a new account via OAuth signup, then provision an application.
expectations: Ensures the Algolia CLI is installed before authenticating
Uses 'algolia auth signup' because the user has no account yet (not 'algolia auth login')
Explains the OAuth flow opens the browser, and mentions the --no-browser fallback for headless/SSH environments
Provisions an application (either relies on the OAuth flow auto-creating one, or asks the user for a name, region, and plan before running 'algolia application create')
Does NOT pass --accept-terms without explicit user confirmation of the plan's terms

evals.prompt: I already have an Algolia account and a couple of applications. Authenticate me and switch to the right application, but I don't remember the exact app names.
evals.expected_output: Log in via OAuth, list applications, prompt the user to choose, then select it.
expectations: Uses 'algolia auth login' (not signup) because the user already has an account
Uses 'algolia application list --output json' to enumerate the available applications
Prompts the user to pick an application rather than choosing one automatically
Uses 'algolia application select --app-name <chosen_name>' to switch to it

evals.prompt: I'm setting up Algolia on a remote server over SSH, so I can't open a browser. I have an account already. Create a new free application called 'My Search' in the EU region.
evals.expected_output: Login with --no-browser, then create an application with an explicit name, region, and plan after confirming terms.
expectations: Uses 'algolia auth login --no-browser' since no browser is available over SSH, and shows the printed URL to the user
Uses 'algolia application create' with --name "My Search", --region EU, and --plan free
Confirms the plan's terms of service with the user before passing --accept-terms
Does NOT use 'algolia auth signup' since the user already has an account

evals.prompt: We're starting from nothing — no Algolia account. Our app is a Next.js storefront that we deploy on Vercel. Set Algolia up for us.
evals.expected_output: Recognise the Vercel signal, ask whether Vercel should own the application, and route to algolia-vercel rather than running 'algolia auth signup'.
expectations: Detects that the project ships on Vercel and raises the Vercel Marketplace path before provisioning
Asks the user whether Vercel should own, connect, and bill the Algolia application
Does NOT run 'algolia auth signup' or 'algolia application create' before that answer
Routes to the algolia-vercel skill (offering 'npx skills add algolia/skills --skill algolia-vercel') if the user wants Vercel to own it
Continues with the CLI quickstart only if the user declines the Vercel path

evals.prompt: I have a Next.js app and no Algolia account yet. Get me an App ID and an API key.
evals.expected_output: Next.js alone is not a Vercel signal, so this is the ordinary CLI quickstart; check for a Vercel signal, find none, and proceed.
expectations: Treats Next.js alone as insufficient evidence of Vercel hosting — does not assume the Vercel Marketplace path
Either proceeds with 'algolia auth signup' plus application provisioning, or asks once about the deployment target
Does NOT run 'vercel integration add algolia'
Does not pass --accept-terms without explicit user confirmation

evals.prompt: Provision Algolia for us through the Vercel Marketplace — we want Vercel to own and bill it. No Algolia account yet.
evals.expected_output: The choice is already made. Route straight to algolia-vercel without re-asking for the same approval.
expectations: Routes to algolia-vercel immediately — the user already chose the Vercel Marketplace
Does NOT ask again whether Vercel should own the application
Does NOT run 'algolia auth signup' or 'algolia application create'
Still leaves plan, region, and provider terms as decisions for the user
